data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 asserts Dijkstra's maxim 'tests can show the presence of bugs, not their absence' as support for replacing exact-count assertions with invariant property checks. But this causal mechanism is mismatched: Dijkstra's principle is an epistemic limitation about what testing can prove (it cannot prove absence of bugs), not a directive about avoiding cardinality assertions or preferring property-based tests. A test that pins an exact count of committed artifacts is itself a way of showing the PRESENCE of a bug when the count changes unexpectedly — exactly what Dijkstra says tests can do. The principle provides no causal reason to switch from cardinality to invariants.
